title: Maximal trunk exertions
summary: Simulate maximal isometric trunk exertions in six directions; report primary moment, coupled moments and muscle EMG at MVC.
simulate: Scale the model to the study subject (table below; by sex where given).
Fix pelvis and legs in the task posture (semi-seated, standing, seated or side-lying).
Maximise the moment in the task direction with all muscles free; record moments about the task's reference.
Report primary moment magnitude and the two coupled moments (signed, absolute or % as the output says).
Report each muscle's activation, normalised to its maximum over the six exertions.

notes: Coupled moments use three conventions (signed Nm, absolute Nm, signed % of same-plane MVC): separate outputs, never pooled. Signs: + flexion, + right lateral, + right axial.

Moment reference: L5-S1 (Ghezelbash, El Ouaaid, Larivière, Daggfeldt; Ng and Gravel dynamometer axes at L5-S1) vs vertical axis (McGill, Kumar). EMG references: max over the 6 MVCs; Ng baseline-subtracted.

Excluded: Burkhart 2018 (force at pad), Ng 2002 LBP group, Larivière 2014 (= 2009 sample), submaximal EMG/coupling (Larivière 2001/2009), Kumar EMG and McGill EMG (other references). More postures and sides in raw tests.
agent_prompt: You are validating a trunk musculoskeletal model in maximal isometric exertions. For each task, scale the model to the study subject (`subjects`, by sex where given), fix pelvis and legs in the task posture, and maximise the trunk moment in the task direction (flexion, extension, lateral bend or axial rotation, right/left) with all muscles free. Report moments about the task's moment_ref: the primary moment as a magnitude, and coupled moments about the other two axes as the output requires (signed: + flexion, + right lateral, + right axial; absolute; or signed % of the subject's maximal moment in that plane). For EMG tasks report activation (%) of the muscles under the named electrode, normalised to that muscle's maximum over the six exertions. Do not tune the model to these data. Return one JSON object following answer_format: task id -> {output key: value}.
